disclaimer: Official stop records can be months or years behind. A shaded area is a police beat or a 150 m cell, never one stop. Many places publish no mappable location, so coverage is uneven.
attribution: Stanford Open Policing Project (Open Data Commons Attribution License); City of Urbana open data; NYPD Vehicle Stop Reports (NYC Open Data); Montgomery County electronic traffic violations (dataMontgomery); Champaign, IL police-beat polygons (City of Champaign open data).

sources.name: Stanford Open Policing Project — Chicago
sources.note: Standardized stops, roughly 2012–2016 and 2018–2020. Beat outlines are the project shapefile (ODC-BY). A row with no beat code is placed in the beat polygon that contains its published coordinate, or on the 150 m grid if it falls outside.

sources.name: City of Urbana IDOT stop sheets
sources.license: City of Urbana open data, via data.illinois.gov
sources.note: Stop-sheet rows with a published map point. Points are snapped to the 150 m grid unless they fall inside a Champaign beat polygon. Street addresses are not stored. Geo codes that are not Champaign beat names are not drawn as beats.

sources.name: NYPD Vehicle Stop Reports
sources.license: NYC Open Data (City of New York)
sources.note: Vehicle stops joined to NYPD precinct polygons on the published command code. The coordinate is not stored.

sources.name: Montgomery County, MD electronic traffic violations
sources.note: Geocoded electronic violations, snapped to the 150 m grid. Person and vehicle fields are not requested and not stored.

notMapped.name: Stanford Open Policing Project — Illinois statewide
notMapped.why: About 12 million IDOT-style rows, mostly beat codes without coordinates. No statewide beat polygons are bundled here, so it is not drawn. Pass a beat GeoJSON into a future run if you have one; do not commit the raw file.

notMapped.name: Connecticut traffic stops (data.ct.gov)
notMapped.why: Published rows have a town and an intersection string, not coordinates. Intersections are not geocoded (that would invent precise points). Town-wide shapes are not drawn.

notMapped.name: Stanford Open Policing Project — San Diego
notMapped.why: The standardized file has a service-area code and no coordinates. The project shapefile is nine police divisions and does not use those codes, so it is not drawn.

notMapped.name: San Diego RIPA stops
notMapped.why: Quarterly files include a beat name and a street block, not latitude/longitude. Block addresses are not geocoded and are not stored.
